featureSummary: Multi-tenant ops software for small 3PL teams running warehouse, fleet, and crew for live events—built so gear stays locked to the job until load-out.
caseStudyIntro: Logiparty is a multi-tenant web app for third-party logistics companies that run warehouse, fleet, and crew for live events, deliveries, and corporate jobs. Each company gets its own workspace on its own subdomain and a white-label portal where clients request jobs and see only their inventory. The product treats the job as the unit of work: trucks, crew, and client-owned gear stay tied to that job until load-out releases them.

caseStudyFacts.label: Tenancy
caseStudyFacts.teaser: One platform, many isolated company workspaces.
caseStudyFacts.detail: Each 3PL runs on its own subdomain with branded login and email. Database isolation keeps one company’s jobs, inventory, and documents out of another’s view.

caseStudyFacts.label: Jobs
caseStudyFacts.teaser: Inventory, fleet, crew, locations, and paperwork on one record.
caseStudyFacts.detail: A job carries client inventory lines, vehicles, crew assignments, up to five locations, and uploaded documents. Status moves from draft through upcoming and ready to completed—or denied when a request does not fit.

caseStudyFacts.label: Locks
caseStudyFacts.teaser: Gear and trucks stay reserved while work is upcoming or ready.
caseStudyFacts.detail: Client inventory and fleet units lock to the job so double-booking shows up in the system instead of on a spreadsheet. Load-out releases them for the next job.

caseStudyFacts.label: Client portal
caseStudyFacts.teaser: End clients request work without seeing the operator’s whole warehouse.
caseStudyFacts.detail: Invite-only roles separate org staff from client users. Clients submit job requests, attach files, and track their own inventory—not another brand’s catalog.

caseStudySteps.title: Inventory locks
caseStudySteps.body: When a job is upcoming or ready, the inventory and vehicles assigned to it are reserved. Staff see what is spoken for before they promise the same gear elsewhere.

caseStudySteps.title: Crew & trucks
caseStudySteps.body: Managers assign load-in and load-out crew, drivers, and fleet to the job. The record becomes the single place to see who and what is attached before anyone leaves the warehouse.

caseStudySteps.title: Load-out
caseStudySteps.body: After load-out, locks release. Inventory and vehicles return to the available pool so the next job can be built without manual cleanup in side channels.

caseStudyStack: Next.js on Vercel, Neon Postgres with row-level security, wildcard DNS for per-company subdomains, auth with role-based access, Cloudflare R2 for private documents with signed URLs, and branded transactional email. The architecture is built for isolation first, then features on top.
caseStudyProcess: I shaped the product direction and system design, wrote implementation briefs for coding agents, reviewed diffs and production behavior, and kept ownership of what ships. The case study focuses on the product; the process is simply how this codebase stayed coherent while moving fast.
